Looking at the front view, all three vases have the same width, and the water heights satisfy: h(II) > h(I) > h(III).

The volume of water in each vase equals width × depth × water height, where the depth is what we see as the vertical dimension in the top view.

**Comparing I and III:** Both hold 4 L, but vase I has a higher water level than vase III. So vase I must have a smaller depth: depth(I) < depth(III).

**Comparing II and I:** Vase II holds less water (3 L vs 4 L) yet shows a higher water level. So vase II must have a clearly smaller depth: depth(II) < depth(I).

**Combining:** depth(II) < depth(I) < depth(III).

The top view must therefore show three rectangles of equal width whose heights (depths) are: II smallest, I medium, III largest. Only image (A) matches this ordering.

\boxed{A}
